decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “first release covers saving”; Round 1 client discusses pasting a link without disputing URL-based saving.
decisions.note: The proposed save-by-link behavior conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “covers … opening”; Round 1 client requests no change to opening bookmarks.
decisions.note: Opening a saved bookmark is a conforming specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “covers … editing”; Round 1 client retains editing and asks that retrieved title or description remain adjustable.
decisions.note: The recorded editing capability is conforming; the response refines its interaction with fetched metadata.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “covers … deleting”; Round 1 client does not contest deletion.
decisions.note: Deletion is included at the specification gate and does not diverge.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “covers … tagging”; Round 1 client builds on tags when requesting tag-specific search.
decisions.note: Assignment of tags is a conforming proposed behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “covers … filtering”; Round 5 maker later explicitly reports “Tag filters,” which the client accepts after testing.
decisions.note: The recorded tag-filter capability conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “covers … sorting”; Round 5 maker reports “Tag filters and sorting,” with final client acceptance.
decisions.note: Sorting is a conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “without … automatic page metadata.” Round 1 client: “That's not what I want… fetch the page's title (and ideally its description and little site icon) … Please fold that in.”
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, manual metadata entry contradicted automatic collection; the client rejected it and supplied replacement behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents generic “searching.” Round 1 client: “I want to be able to search my tags specifically.”
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, the presented search scope lacked tag-specific search and the client requested the missing requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents generic “searching.” Round 1 client: “if I put something in quotes I'd expect it to find that exact phrase.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing exact-phrase behavior at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only generic searching. Round 1 client requests combinations such as “Rome that's tagged either article or book” and says search must support “that kind of combining.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the initially plain search scope by requesting composable text/tag conditions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's first-release list omits read-later state. Round 1 client: “mark a link as ‘read this later’.”
decisions.note: The client requested the missing unread/read-later state at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's first-release list omits an unread perspective. Round 1 client: “pull up just those unread ones on their own.”
decisions.note: The client requested a dedicated unread view.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's first-release list omits read-state transitions. Round 1 client: “check them off once I've read them.”
decisions.note: The client requested the missing mark-as-read behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client identifies the presented behavior: “warning me and sending me to the existing bookmark instead of making a copy — is exactly right, so keep that.” Round 2 maker confirms it was “retained unchanged.”
decisions.note: The initial duplicate-save decision conforms by directing the user to the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly scopes the release “without … imports.” In Round 5 the client names “importing my existing browser bookmarks” but says it is “for another round” and “doesn't hold up today's version.”
decisions.note: The persistent import exclusion is an accepted divergence: the client explicitly states the missing expectation and accepts deferral.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker revises collection to “page title, description, and site icon,” omitting the required preview image. Round 2 client approves and repeats only “title, description, and site icon.”
decisions.note: The revised specification adds three metadata fields but still omits automatic preview-image collection; the client does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Editable retrieved title and description before and after saving.” Round 2 client: “I can adjust them if I want.”
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms on editing collected title and description before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Tag-specific search”; Round 2 client confirms “searching by tag.”
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms on tag-search syntax/functionality.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Exact-phrase searches using quotation marks”; Round 2 client confirms “exact phrases in quotes.”
decisions.note: The revised exact-phrase behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker offers “multiple tag alternatives” and “combined text, phrase, and tag conditions,” but does not provide the reference's full AND/OR/NOT, parenthesized-group, and quoted-literal-operator behavior. Round 2 client approves only the Rome plus article-or-book example.
decisions.note: At the revised-specification gate, the search language remains narrower than the reference; the client does not identify the missing NOT/general grouping/literal-operator rules.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Read-later collection with explicit read/unread status”; Round 2 client calls it “exactly the deliberate reading queue I had in mind.”
decisions.note: The revised read-later marking behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Dedicated unread read-later view”; Round 2 client approves the read-later list.
decisions.note: The dedicated unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specifies “explicit read/unread status”; Round 2 client approves “marking things read or unread.”
decisions.note: The revised read-state transition conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Original duplicate-bookmark handling retained unchanged”; Round 2 client: “Good that the duplicate handling stayed the same.”
decisions.note: The revised specification preserves the conforming duplicate-save behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker implements “Automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval,” again omitting preview images. Round 5 client tests title/description/icon behavior and accepts the application without mentioning preview images.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the delivered metadata behavior still lacks preview-image collection and the client does not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: “Duplicate detection.” Round 5 client observes that a repeated address “warned me it was already there and pointed me to the one I'd already saved instead of making a copy.”
decisions.note: The implemented duplicate flow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker implements “tag searches”; Round 5 client confirms “searching by tag” returned the right result.
decisions.note: The implemented tag search conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker implements “Exact phrases”; Round 5 client confirms “an exact phrase in quotes” worked.
decisions.note: The implemented exact-phrase behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker claims generic “combined queries” but presents no NOT support or complete parenthesized/quoted-operator grammar. Round 5 client tests only “Example with either the article or book tag” and accepts.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation preserves the narrower combined-query behavior; the unimplemented portions of the reference grammar are not surfaced by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: “Read-later … workflows”; Round 5 client confirms the read-later list and ability to flip an item back to unread.
decisions.note: The implemented unread marking behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker implements read-later workflows; Round 5 client: “The read-later list showed only my unread items.”
decisions.note: The implemented unread-only perspective conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker implements “read/unread workflows”; Round 5 client: “marking one as read dropped it off that list while keeping it in my library.”
decisions.note: The implemented mark-as-read behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “Editing”; Round 5 client states “Editing … worked.”
decisions.note: The delivered editing decision is recorded as conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “confirmed deletion”; Round 5 client states “the confirm-before-delete … worked.”
decisions.note: The delivered permanent-delete behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: The Round 5 maker's completed-feature presentation contains no page snapshot capability. Round 5 client identifies “keeping a saved copy of a page in case it disappears” but explicitly says it is “for another round” and “doesn't hold up today's version.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client explicitly identifies and accepts deferral of local page preservation.
